'''Robert Edward Corbett''' (13 June 1923 – 3 February 2018) was a New Zealand [[organic chemist]]. He is noted for his contribution to [[natural product chemistry]] through the isolation and structural elucidation of compounds from [[New Zealand native plants]].

==Early life and education==
Born on 13 June 1923,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bdmhistoricalrecords.dia.govt.nz/Search/Search?Path=%2FqueryEntry.m%3Ftype%3Ddeaths|title=Death search: registration number 2018/3699 |date= |website=Births, deaths & marriages online |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref> Corbett was the son of Walter Corbett and Margaret Whitehead Corbett (née Robertson). He studied at the [[University of Otago]], graduating [[Master of Science]] with first-class honours in chemistry in 1945.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university6.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Co–Cu |date= |website=Shadows of Time |publisher= |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref> Corbett later undertook doctoral studies at the [[University of Cambridge]] under [[Alexander R. Todd|Alexander Todd]] on the structures of some of the metabolites—puberulic acid, puberulonic acid, and [[stipitatic acid]]—of ''[[Penicillium]]'' species.<ref name="RSNZ">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/members/memberpage/63 |title=Professor Edward Corbett |date= |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref> He showed that they contain the [[tropolone]] skeleton,<ref name="RSNZ"/> and his PhD thesis, titled ''The structure of certain antibiotics'' was completed in 1950.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://explore.bl.uk/BLVU1:LSCOP-ALL:BLL01016703963 |title=Catalogue search |date= |website=British Library |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref>

In 1949, Corbett married Enid Mary Carter in [[Cambridge]], England,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://search.ancestry.com.au/cgi-bin/sse.dll?indiv=try&db=ONSmarriage1984&h=27344962 |title=England & Wales, civil registration marriage index, 1916–2005 |year=2010 |website= |publisher=Ancestry.com Operations |accessdate=13 February 2018 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and they went on to have two children.<ref name="Death notice">{{cite news | url=http://notices.nzherald.co.nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/obituary.aspx?n=robert-edward-corbett-ted&pid=188080239 | title=Professor Robert Edward (Ted) Corbett death notice | date=6 February 2018 | work=[[New Zealand Herald]] | accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="Enid Corbett death notice">{{cite news |url=https://www.sunlive.co.nz/news/30042-corbett-enid-mary.html |title=Corbett, Enid Mary |date=16 August 2012 |work=SunLive |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref>

==Academic and research career==
In 1945, Corbett was appointed as a lecturer in chemistry at Otago.<ref name="Otago calendar">{{cite book |chapter=Emeritus professors |title=University of Otago Calendar |url=http://www.otago.ac.nz/study/otago628508.pdf |accessdate=13 February 2018 |year=2017 |publisher=University of Otago |location=Dunedin |page=121 |archive-date=7 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407053935/http://www.otago.ac.nz/study/otago628508.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> After returning from Cambridge in 1950,<ref name="RSNZ"/> Corbett rose to become a professor in 1966, and the [[Joseph William Mellor|Mellor Professor of Chemistry]] in 1972.<ref name="Otago calendar"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://otago.ourheritage.ac.nz/items/show/9051 |title=Robert E. Corbett |date= |website=Otago University Research Heritage |publisher=University of Otago |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref> When he retired in 1983, he was accorded the title of [[professor emeritus]].<ref name="Otago calendar"/>

Corbett's research at Otago was primarily concerned with the study and structural elucidation of essential oils isolated from New Zealand native plants by steam distillation. Under his supervision in 1970, doctoral student Denis Lauren first isolated the [[diterpene]] compound from the rimu tree (''[[Dacrydium cupressinum]]'') that came to be known as [[laurenene]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://teara.govt.nz/en/photograph/14461/rimu-leaves |title=Rimu leaves |first=Nigel |last=Perry |date=24 September 2007 |website=[[Te Ara – the Encyclopedia of New Zealand]] |publisher=Ministry for Culture and Heritage |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.otago.ac.nz/otagobulletin/news/otago354005.html |title=History of chemistry adorns site hoardings |date=1 December 2015 |publisher=University of Otago |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/chemical-bling-shows-way |title= Chemical bling shows the way |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=15 February 2018 |first=John |last=Gibb |accessdate=15 February 2018}}</ref> Corbett also investigated extractives from barks, leaves, heartwoods and lichens, and determined the structures of many new, and derivatives of known, [[diterpenoid|di-]], [[triterpenoid|tri-]] and [[sesquiterpenoid]]s.<ref name="RSNZ"/> He also studied the synthesis and rearrangement of some of the compounds that his team isolated.<ref name="RSNZ"/>

==Later life and death==
In retirement, the Corbetts lived in [[Tauranga]]. Enid Corbett died there in 2012,<ref name="Enid Corbett death notice"/> and Ted Corbett died on 3 February 2018, also in Tauranga.<ref name="Death notice"/>

==Honours and awards==
In 1972, Corbett was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref name="Fellows">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/a-c/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames A–C |date= |website= |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=13 February 2018}}</ref> He was also a Fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry.<ref name="Otago calendar"/>
